posts.text: A general rule of thumb for bad media ownership situations is that everything is set against an attention market of growing competition / falling demand, and the Wall Street vampires know how to still eke out margins in that game while the vanity billionaires from outside the sector, um, don’t.

A general rule of thumb for bad media ownership situations is that everything is set against an attention market of growing competition / falling demand, and the Wall Street vampires know how to still eke out margins in that game while the vanity billionaires from outside the sector, um, don’t.

This is also where I’m a bit bearish on the left-antitrustish critiques of the whole situation, in that the insanely competitive media environment gives CBS viewers an infinite amount of other things they can do with their time than spend an hour with an obviously deteriorating product.
